name: Aloo Gobi

ingredients.name: Cauliflower (phool gobi), florets
ingredients.householdMeasure: about 1½ cups bite-size florets (¼ medium head)

ingredients.name: Potato (aloo)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium potato, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or mustard oil / groundnut oil)

equipment: Small kadai or heavy frying pan (7–8 inch) with a lid
Large bowl for washing the cauliflower, plus a colander or strainer
Measuring spoons (normal teaspoons are a fine stand-in)
Kitchen towel to dry the vegetables
Small bowl for the powdered spices

steps.title: Cut the cauliflower into florets
steps.text: Pull off the leaves, cut the head into quarters and cut one quarter (about 150 g of florets) into bite-size florets, about 3–4 cm across. Slice thick stems into thin rounds; they are edible.
steps.tip: Make the florets about the same size as the potato cubes, or slightly larger; cauliflower cooks faster than potato.
steps.visualCue: Even, bite-size florets of similar size, so they cook at the same speed.
steps.cameraCheck: The pile of florets on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife cutting a cauliflower quarter into small florets.

steps.title: Soak the florets in warm salted water
steps.text: Put the florets in a bowl, cover with warm water and add ½ tsp salt (extra, mostly drained away). Leave for 5 minutes while you prep everything else.
steps.tip: Indian cauliflower often hides small green worms inside the florets; this soak is how most home cooks clean it.
steps.visualCue: Any tiny worms or dirt float up or settle at the bottom.
steps.cameraCheck: The florets soaking in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Florets dropping into a bowl of steaming water.

steps.title: Peel and cube the potato
steps.text: Peel 1 medium potato (120 g) and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Keep the cubes in a bowl of water so they don't brown.
steps.videoShot: The knife cubing a peeled potato.

steps.title: Chop the aromatics
steps.text: Finely chop the onion (40 g), tomato (50 g), ginger (1 tsp), garlic (1 clove) and green chilli.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces; the tomato is in small dice.
steps.cameraCheck: Small heaps of onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: Overhead shot of the chopped heaps.

steps.title: Mix the powdered spices
steps.text: In a small bowl, put ⅛ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¾ tsp coriander powder. Keep the garam masala, amchur and kasuri methi separately for the end.
steps.visualCue: A small mound of red, yellow and brown powders.
steps.videoShot: The three powders spooned into a bowl.

steps.title: Drain and dry the vegetables
steps.text: Drain the cauliflower, rinse once under the tap, and drain the potato. Spread both on a kitchen towel and pat dry.
steps.tip: Wet vegetables steam instead of browning and make the oil splutter.
steps.visualCue: No water dripping; surfaces look only slightly damp.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained florets and cubes on a towel
steps.videoShot: Hands patting the vegetables dry in a towel.

steps.title: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat, add 2 tsp (10 ml) oil, then ½ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black straight away, the oil is too hot; take the pan off the heat for a few seconds. If using mustard oil, heat it until it just starts to smoke, then let it cool for 30 seconds before adding the cumin.
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles, darkens one shade and smells toasty within about 20 seconds.
steps.videoShot: Cumin seeds sizzling in shimmering oil.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The onion turns soft, translucent and just light golden at the edges.
steps.videoShot: The spatula stirring onions that are turning golden.

steps.title: Add the ginger, garlic and green chilli
steps.visualCue: The raw smell of garlic goes, replaced by a fragrant, sharp aroma.
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with onion, ginger, garlic and chilli

steps.title: Add the potato cubes
steps.text: Add the potato, stir to coat in the oil, and fry uncovered on medium heat, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: Potato goes in before the cauliflower because it takes longer to cook. This is the main step most recipes agree on.
steps.visualCue: The potato edges look slightly translucent and a few corners start to turn golden.
steps.cameraCheck: The potato cubes in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Potatoes tossing in the onion mixture.

steps.title: Add the cauliflower
steps.text: Add the florets and stir gently to mix.
steps.visualCue: The florets are coated in oil and a few spots on them start to turn light golden.
steps.cameraCheck: The potato and cauliflower together in the kadai
steps.videoShot: Florets going into the kadai and being folded in.

steps.title: Add the spice powders and salt
steps.text: Turn the heat to low. Add the spice bowl (turmeric, chilli, coriander powder) and ⅓ tsp salt. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
steps.tip: On low heat the powders roast without burning. If the pan looks dry and spices stick, add 1 tbsp water.
steps.visualCue: Every piece looks evenly yellow-orange; the spices smell roasted, not burnt.
steps.videoShot: Spices being sprinkled over and the vegetables turning yellow.

steps.title: Add the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and stir.
steps.visualCue: The tomato starts to soften and release a little juice.
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato on top of the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Tomato dice tumbling into the kadai.

steps.title: Sprinkle water and cover
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp water around the edges of the pan, cover with the lid and cook on low heat.
steps.tip: Stir by lifting from underneath, not mashing. If the bottom sticks, add 1 more tbsp water. Do not add more than 3 tbsp in total, or it turns into a curry.
steps.visualCue: Steam builds under the lid; the tomato melts into a thick coating on the vegetables.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered kadai, then the vegetables when you lift the lid
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off to release steam.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.text: Press a potato cube and a cauliflower stem piece with the spatula or a knife.
steps.tip: If the potato is still hard, cover and cook 2–3 min more. If the cauliflower is getting soft first, cook uncovered instead.
steps.visualCue: The potato breaks easily; the cauliflower is tender but still holds its shape with a slight bite.
steps.cameraCheck: A potato cube and a floret on the spatula, pressed
steps.videoShot: A knife sliding into a potato cube.

steps.title: Dry it out and brown lightly
steps.text: Remove the lid, turn the heat to medium and cook uncovered, stirring gently every minute.
steps.visualCue: No liquid left at the bottom; the vegetables look dry, glossy and have a few golden-brown patches.
steps.cameraCheck: The dry sabzi in the kadai
steps.videoShot: The vegetables sizzling with no liquid in the pan.

steps.title: Add the finishing spices
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala, ¼ tsp amchur and ½ tsp crushed kasuri methi (rub it between your palms). Add the chopped coriander leaves. Toss gently.
steps.visualCue: Flecks of green and brown over the sabzi; it smells warm and slightly tangy.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished aloo gobi with coriander on top
steps.videoShot: Kasuri methi being crushed between palms over the pan.

steps.title: Taste and serve
steps.text: Taste a piece and adjust with a pinch of salt or amchur. Cover for 2 minutes so the flavours settle, then serve in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Golden-yellow, dry, chunky sabzi with soft potatoes and just-tender cauliflower.
steps.videoShot: Aloo gobi spooned into a bowl next to a hot roti.

reasons: a vegetable-only dish with just 2 tsp oil, no frying, no cream and a good 8–9 g of fibre per bowl; cauliflower adds vitamin C and the spices add flavour without calories. Points come off because protein is low (about 7 g) and potato makes it starch-heavy, so it needs dal, curd or paneer alongside to be a full meal. Restaurant and dhaba versions often deep-fry the potato and cauliflower first or use 1 tbsp+ of oil or ghee per portion, plus more salt.

researchRating.basis: aloo gobi is one of North India's most-cooked everyday sabzis and a well-known Punjabi home dish (it even features in pop culture, e.g. the film Bend It Like Beckham). Recipes are very well reviewed (Swasthi's Recipes 4.98/5 from 630 votes; Vegan Richa's restaurant-style aloo gobi has several pages of reader comments; Veg Recipes of India's version has 8+ comment pages; Tarla Dalal's dry aloo gobi has about 694,000 views). Small deduction because it is seen as a simple, everyday dish, and some people find it bland or mushy when overcooked.

storage: Refrigerate in an airtight box within 2 hours of cooking. It keeps for 2 days in the fridge (the cauliflower smell gets stronger after that). Freezing is not recommended; potatoes turn grainy and the cauliflower watery when thawed. To reheat, sprinkle 1 tsp water and microwave covered for 1–1½ min, or warm in a pan on low heat for 3–4 min, stirring gently, until steaming hot.
leftoverRemix: Aloo gobi paratha (or toastie). Mash 1 cup leftover aloo gobi with a fork, add 1 tbsp chopped onion and a pinch of chaat masala. Stuff it into rolled-out wheat dough and cook on a tawa with ½ tsp oil per side until golden spots appear. Or spread it between two slices of bread with a slice of cheese and toast it in a sandwich maker for a quick breakfast.
burnOff: about 3.8 km of running (265 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.3 km of brisk walking (about 65 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). This is for the sabzi alone; 2 phulkas would add about 2–2.5 km of running.
